Treatment summary
Patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the patient's vehicle was struck from the side while the
patient was turning left. The patient reports low back pain and stiffness beginning at the time of the impact, which is a
plausible mechanism for a strain of this kind. No prior injury to the lumbar region is known to this provider, and the
patient denied earlier episodes of back trouble.
Diagnosis is lumbar strain. Lumbar imaging was obtained and showed no acute fracture, malalignment, or other
abnormality, and neurological and musculoskeletal examination fnidings were within normal limits. Because objective
findings were unremarkable, the diagnosis rests largely on the patient's own description of pain and functional
limitation.
Care consisetd of 23 visits including manual therapy, graded stretching and strengthening exercise, and home
exercise instruction. Treatment followed a typical course for a soft tissue injury, with frequency decreasing as
symptoms improved. At the most recent visit the patient reported substantial improvement and was discharged to
self-directed home exercise. Billing records reflect each service once as scheduled, with no duplicate or repeated
charges for the same encounter.
</page>
